newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia optimistic on gas sale to German firms.
newsitem.headline: Latvia optimistic on gas sale to German firms.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday that Preussen and Ruhrgas are expected finally to agree to buy a stake in Latvian Gas but problems have emerged with Gazprom's part in the sale.
The German companies are due to make a decision on Latvian Gas by Friday.
They have held back from committing themselves earlier due to worries over the gas company's debts.
Preussen and Ruhrgas formed a consortium to buy a stake in Latvian Gas while Russia's Gazprom was taking part as a separate partner.
"Gazprom at the moment has postponed its wish to buy a stake in Latvian Gas," LPA chief Janis Naglis told a seminar on Latvia's capital markets.
He did not give any information on Gazprom's reasons for becoming reluctant to take part in the privatisation.

"More hopeful information, following a telephone conversation, shows that we can expect a positive decision about their (Ruhrgas and Preussen) participation in the privatisation in a month's time," Naglis added.
The Latvian side had earlier offered to guarantee some of the debts of Latvian Gas but not all.
Naglis said that as soon as the strategic investors have bought their stake, 15 percent of shares will be sold in a public offering, to take place in May or June.
French state-owned Gaz de France may be offered the stake in Latvian Gas if the German firms pull out, the LPA has said.
